description: Agent Pay Phase 2.5 (docs/ai-architecture/mastercard-agent-pay.md): synthetic agent repositories, one file each, and the payment-capability fact the reference scanner's code source must report for each. The sources are data: written to a temporary directory and read statically, never imported or run.

cases.why: x402's fetch wrapper, the 1.x package
x402's axios interceptor, the 1.x package
the 2.x scoped package, reached through a namespace import
the 2.x scoped axios package, through require()
the Python SDK's httpx client, as a context manager

files.shop/agent.py:
from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from x402.http.clients.httpx import x402HttpxClient

async def buy(url):
    async with x402HttpxClient(account=None, base_url=url) as client:  # PAY
        return await client.get("/resource")

agent = create_react_agent(ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini"), [])

cases.why: the Python SDK's requests session, under the 1.x module path

cases.why: the Python payer client, reached as an attribute of the module

files.shop/agent.py:
from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
import x402

payer = x402.x402Client()  # PAY

agent = create_react_agent(ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini"), [])

cases.why: an alias is a capability where it is made
an import that is never called or bound is no payment path
a dynamic import behind a variable in a payment-naming file stops the read vouching for the file
importlib in a payment-naming file, with a computed module name

files.shop/agent.py:
from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
import importlib

payments = importlib.import_module("x402" + ".http.clients")

agent = create_react_agent(ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini"), [])

cases.why: a literal dynamic import of a payment module still hides which member is called
a local function with the client's name is not x402's
the seller side accepts payments and initiates none
a literal dynamic import of a non-payment module is ordinary code
`from importlib import import_module` makes the call a bare name; a literal payment module behind it is out of sight

files.shop/agent.py:
from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from importlib import import_module

m = import_module("x402.clients")
client = m.x402HttpxClient()

agent = create_react_agent(ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini"), [])

cases.why: `getattr(x402, "x402Client")` reaches the entry point by a literal name, so it is a capability

files.shop/agent.py:
from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
import x402

fn = getattr(x402, "x402Client")
client = fn()

agent = create_react_agent(ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini"), [])

cases.why: `getattr` on a payment module with a computed name is out of sight

files.shop/agent.py:
from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
import os
import x402

fn = getattr(x402, os.environ["PAY_CLIENT"])

agent = create_react_agent(ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini"), [])

cases.why: an entry point held as an object's value is a capability where it is held
an entry point passed to another function is a capability at the call
an agent file that loads a module named at run time is out of sight, whether or not it spells a payment library
